title: Session cookie attached to a request for an unrelated collector
description: A live session cookie is attached to a request sent to an unrelated collector host, so a bearer credential leaves the application it authenticates to.
notes: Pairs with header-benign-auth-001 and header-benign-cookies-002, which allow the same cookie shape because a session cookie returned to the application it belongs to is ordinary traffic. The discriminator is destination, not shape. An earlier draft of this case carried a Referer naming the application the session belonged to; it was removed rather than explained. A request header is written by the sender, so a control that reads origin out of Referer is reading a value the sender chose, and the case would have been scoring that mistake. Nothing else in a request Cookie header states which host the session belongs to, so the only sound basis available here is the destination itself. An agent is not a browser and applies no same-origin rule of its own, which is why the crossing has to be caught at the proxy.
source: RFC 6265 cookie scope; session credential leaving its application through an agent-issued request
